stories.title: D11 Considers $775 Million Bond Measure — Board Votes August 5
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Colorado Springs School District 11 is weighing a $775 million bond measure, its first bond in more than 20 years (the last passed in 2004). The D11 board votes August 5 on whether to place the bond on the November ballot. The measure would fund air conditioning for schools 50 to 100 years old and includes teacher pay increases. Estimated tax impact: approximately $6.50 per month per $100,000 of property value. D11 serves the central Colorado Springs area. Sources: Colorado Springs Gazette (July 29, 2026), KRDO, KOAA.

stories.title: Five CPSC Recalls Affecting Children's Products — Summer 2026 Safety Roundup
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Five children's product recalls issued or confirmed this summer warrant attention before families gear up for back-to-school. Babypark 3-in-1 infant/toddler carriers (suffocation risk — leg openings too large); POPOOO/Delightmi Jungle Safari LED Finger Lights (button cell battery access); TOMY Boon PIVOT toddler tower/kitchen step stools (shifting and leaning risk, 11 reports, sold at Target/Amazon/Babylist); Target Gigglescape Under the Sea Popping Toys (dome detaches exposing small choking-hazard balls, 9 reports including 1 choking); Peony Design personalized baby bibs/stroller bags (snap can detach, choking risk). Sources: CPSC.gov, Medical Daily, The BayNet.

research.facts:
CPSC Summer 2026 Children's Product Recalls
**HIGH confidence facts:**
**Babypark 3-in-1 Soft Infant/Toddler Carriers:**
- Hazard: leg openings too large — suffocation/fall risk for infants
- Sold: Amazon.com, approximately April 2024–May 2026
- Action: stop use immediately; contact seller for refund
research.sources:
- Source: CPSC.gov
**POPOOO/Delightmi Jungle Safari LED Finger Lights:**
- Hazard: accessible button cell battery compartment — ingestion risk for young children
- Sold: approximately July 2025–April 2026
- Action: keep away from children; contact seller
- Source: CPSC.gov
**TOMY Boon PIVOT Toddler Tower/Kitchen Step Stools:**
- Hazard: product shifts and leans when child is on it — fall risk; 11 reports of incidents
- Sold: Target.com, Amazon, Babylist; January 2023–June 2026
- Action: stop use; contact TOMY/Boon for remedy
- Source: CPSC.gov, Medical Daily
**Target Gigglescape Under the Sea Popping Toys:**
- Hazard: dome detaches, exposing small balls — choking hazard; 9 reports including 1 choking incident
- Sold: Target stores and Target.com
- Action: stop use; return to Target for refund
- Source: CPSC.gov
**Peony Design Personalized Baby Bibs/Stroller Bags:**
- Recall date: July 23, 2026
- Hazard: snap can detach from fabric — choking hazard for infants
- Action: stop use; contact Peony Design for refund
- Source: CPSC.gov
**Sources:** CPSC.gov (multiple recall pages), Medical Daily, The BayNet, getkeptapp.com

stories.title: Colorado's Gov. Polis Among Six Governors Urging AAP to Add Early Math to Well-Child Visits
stories.angle: FOLLOW-UP / EXPANDED (July 28 Story 4 covered this story; new angle for July 30: what COS parents can do now) — On July 23, 2026, six governors — including Colorado's Jared Polis — sent a letter to the American Academy of Pediatrics urging formal early numeracy guidance modeled on the AAP's existing literacy program. The practical angle for COS families: ask your child's pediatrician about early math milestones at your next well-child visit. Counting, sorting, and simple number games build the numeracy skills that predict long-term academic success. This is especially timely with D49's first day of school four days away.
